GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-03-14T19:05:20Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Merge delay error for multiple API calls.
Description: ```
launchJob {
            Observable.mergeDelayError(
                    getCareUseCase.getAllGetCareItems().toObservable(),
                    appointmentUseCase.getAllAppointment().toObservable()
                        .mergeWith(
                            prescriptionRefillsUseCase.getAllPrescriptionRefills())
                            .mergeWith(billUseCase.getAllPayBills())
                        .mergeWith(careTeamUseCase.getMyCareTeam())
                        .mergeWith(favoriteFacilitiesUseCase.getAllFavoriteFacilities())
                ).iOSubscribeMainThreadObserve()
                .subscribe({
                    mapSection(it)
                    flattenAndEmit()
                }, {
                   Log.e(TAG, "Failed to load dashboard contents")
                })
        }


```

If any of the API is failing entire stream is failing.  Any one knows why?

This is my requirement, I want to make all the API calls parallel,  I don't care about the order in which response arrives, I don't care if one fails, which one come fast, I just display in the order that receives.

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about RxJava's mergeDelayError operator not working as expected when making multiple API calls in parallel. The user is experiencing that when one API call fails, the entire stream fails, despite using mergeDelayError which should allow other streams to complete even when one fails.

This is a conceptual issue related to how RxJava operators work. The solution would involve explaining the correct usage of mergeDelayError and possibly suggesting code modifications like:
1. Ensuring each individual stream has proper error handling
2. Using onErrorResumeNext or onErrorReturn on individual streams
3. Checking if the mergeDelayError is being applied at the correct level in the chain

No build environment is needed to analyze this code and provide a solution. An LLM can identify the issue in the RxJava chain structure and suggest corrections based on RxJava's documented behavior. The solution can be verified through code analysis without needing to run the code, as it's about the proper application of reactive programming patterns.
